card.title: Back My Version
card.instruction: Recruit someone to remember, repeat, and defend one shared version of events when questions begin.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The caretaker's asking about our extra key. Tell him we were checking the cake cupboard's lock.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We did check it. Then we ate the cake.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Start with the part we both remember as maintenance.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He'll ask why there are crumbs in the lock.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we both remember a blockage. Say that back so we're consistent.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 tells B what to repeat; A3 frames shared memory as maintenance and A5 requires B to say the blockage version back.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 admits eating cake, so A3 selects maintenance; B4 crumbs in the lock become A5 a blockage explanation.

relationship.evidence: B2 admits what happened and B4 anticipates the caretaker's evidence question, plausibly testing the story.

heightening.evidence: B4 physical evidence threatens the account; A5 converts it into support and demands rehearsal.

specificity.evidence: A1 caretaker, extra key and cake cupboard establish an immediate accountability conversation.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 blockage turns incriminating crumbs into the very maintenance problem their story claims.
